charmDescription: A tiny glass orb containing a faint blue glow — the simplest element captured as light
alchemicalNote: The first element — the star's fuel. The Constant carries starlight; hydrogen is what stars burn. The beginning of all chains.

charmDescription: A tiny glass orb that floats slightly — lighter than air, glowing pale yellow in the cosmology dark
alchemicalNote: The second element — the product of hydrogen fusion in stars. The Cosmology level's first charm.

charmDescription: A tiny silvery casting, very light, slightly warm to the touch
alchemicalNote: The lightest metal. Found in lepidolite — the calming stone. Lithium grounds the nervous system as it grounds the crystal lattice.

charmDescription: A small steel-grey casting, deceptively light, with a subtle bluish undertone
alchemicalNote: The element of beryl — emerald and aquamarine grow from beryllium. The Siren's deep-water eye color is cobalt, but the stone that carries the water is beryl.

charmDescription: A dark crystal point, nearly black, with a glassy luster
alchemicalNote: The element that colors tourmaline — the watermelon stone. Boron creates the pink, green, and blue zones in tourmaline crystals.

charmDescription: A small crystal point that shifts between graphite grey and diamond clarity depending on the light
connectedStones: Diamond, graphite, coal; also all organic stones (amber, jet, pearl)
alchemicalNote: The element of life and the element of diamonds. The coal-to-diamond alchemical metaphor. The building system: Wood = C + H + O. The most versatile element in the Inn.

charmDescription: A tiny glass orb with a clear, colorless contents — 78% of the air, invisible and essential
connectedStones: None (atmospheric gas; nitrogen compounds in saltpeter)
alchemicalNote: The element of air. The breathing mechanic. The neuro-accessible calm — nitrogen's role in decompression, the deep-water diving connection.

charmDescription: A tiny glass orb with a faint blue tint — the element of breath and rust
connectedStones: Most oxide minerals (hematite, quartz SiO2, corundum Al2O3, etc.)
alchemicalNote: The element of breath and oxidation. The water system (H2O). The oxidation of metals — rust, patina, the aging of copper. The living forest breathes oxygen.

charmDescription: A pale crystal point, nearly colorless, with a sharp angular form — the most reactive element
alchemicalNote: The element of fluorite — the Fae Kingdom's reward stone. Fluorite's fluorescence (glow under UV) is named after fluorine. The element that makes stones glow.

charmDescription: A tiny glass orb that glows orange-red when the cosmology level is dark
alchemicalNote: The noble gas that lights the dark. The cosmology level's signage — the star-labels are neon glows.

charmDescription: A soft silver casting that must be kept in oil — reactive, alive, the metal that fizzes in water
alchemicalNote: The element of salt. The body's electrolyte. The preservation of food — salt as the first alchemy. The both are: the adequate — the reactive metal and the stable salt.

charmDescription: A light silver casting that burns white — the element of brilliant flame
connectedStones: Magnesite, dolomite, periclase, talc; also in olivine and pyroxene
alchemicalNote: The element of brilliant white fire. The both are: the adequate — the burning and the structural. Magnesium is in the earth's mantle and in the chlorophyll of the garden.

charmDescription: A light silver casting — the most abundant metal in the earth's crust
connectedStones: Corundum (ruby, sapphire — Al2O3), bauxite, kaolinite, feldspar
alchemicalNote: The element of ruby and sapphire. The most abundant metal in the crust — the element that makes the earth's surface. The both are: the adequate — the common and the precious, the same aluminum, different impurity.

charmDescription: A miniature crystal point — the element of the geode, the Inn's namesake
connectedStones: Quartz, amethyst, citrine, agate, jasper, opal, chalcedony, onyx, tiger's eye, chert, flint, chalcedony
alchemicalNote: THE element of the Inn. Silicon is the geode. Silicon is quartz. Silicon is the crystal that gives the Inn its name. The Heart Crystal is silicon. The both are: the adequate — the crystal and the Inn, the same silicon, different architecture.

charmDescription: A small piece that glows faintly green-white in the dark — the element of light
alchemicalNote: The element of phosphorescence. Bioluminescence — the Atlantis algae glow. The glowing nodes throughout the Inn. The both are: the adequate — the element and the glow, the same light, different source.

charmDescription: A small yellow crystal — the element of brimstone, the devil's element, the alchemist's element
connectedStones: Pyrite (fool's gold), cinnabar (with mercury), gypsum, sulfur crystals, galena (sulfide)
alchemicalNote: The element of brimstone and the alchemist's sulfur. The both are: the adequate — the devil's element and the healer's element. Sulfur connects to the staircase — the transformation through fire. Pyrite (fool's gold) is iron disulfide.

charmDescription: A small green-tinted glass orb — the element of salt's other half, the purifier
alchemicalNote: The element of purification. The both are: the adequate — the purifier and the salt. Chlorine cleans; sodium preserves. The both are: the same salt, different function.

charmDescription: A tiny glass orb with a faint violet glow — the noble gas that fills 1% of the air
alchemicalNote: The noble gas of stillness. Argon does not react. The both are: the adequate — the active and the inert. The cosmology level's silence.

charmDescription: A soft silver casting — the element of the heartbeat, the electrolyte of life
alchemicalNote: The element of the heartbeat. The 50 BPM rhythm depends on potassium. The both are: the adequate — the heartbeat and the earth. Potassium is in every heartbeat and in every feldspar.

charmDescription: A white-grey casting — the element of bone and stone, the architect of bodies and caves
connectedStones: Calcite, limestone, marble, aragonite, fluorite (CaF2), gypsum, apatite
alchemicalNote: The element of bone and stone. The both are: the adequate — the skeleton and the cave. Calcium builds the bones (Marijke's bone art) and builds the caves (limestone, calcite). The building system: limestone + water = mortar. The both are: the adequate.

charmDescription: A light silvery casting with a subtle yellow tint — the rare earth that isn't quite rare earth
alchemicalNote: The bridge between the common transition metals and the rare earths. The both are: the adequate — the between.

charmDescription: A strong, dark silver casting — the element of strength and lightness, the Siren's element
questConnection: Tidal Caves exploration — Wyndham Lewis zone
alchemicalNote: The element of strength and lightness. The Siren's titanium theme — strength that weighs nothing. Rutile: the needle inclusions in quartz (rutilated quartz). The geological orchestra uses titanium's resonance.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that shifts color — grey, green, purple, depending on oxidation state
connectedStones: Vanadinite, carnotite, roscoelite; in some beryl and tourmaline
alchemicalNote: The element of color-shifting. Vanadium makes tsavorite garnet green and some beryl blue. The both are: the adequate — the chameleon element, the Shifting Man's metal.

charmDescription: A hard, mirror-bright silver charm — the element of chrome, the element of vivid color
connectedStones: Chrome diopside, uvarovite garnet, chromite; traces in ruby and emerald (chromium colors both)
questConnection: Poison Garden exploration — English Power Gothic zone
alchemicalNote: The element that colors ruby red and emerald green — the same element, different stone, different color. The both are: the adequate — the red and the green, the same chromium, different host. The Poison Garden's toxic beauty.

charmDescription: A dark grey-black casting — the element that colors stone purple and black
connectedStones: Pyrolusite, rhodochrosite, rhodonite, psilomelane; traces in amethyst (purple)
questConnection: Petrified Forest / crystal chamber — Eileen's cave
alchemicalNote: The element that colors petrified wood black and purple. The both are: the adequate — the dark and the purple. Eileen's cave pigment — manganese black. Amethyst's purple traces manganese.

charmDescription: A dark metallic casting with a reddish-brown undertone — the element of blood and earth
connectedStones: Hematite, magnetite, pyrite, siderite, limonite, goethite, taconite
alchemicalNote: The element of blood and the earth's core. The both are: the adequate — the blood and the stone, the same iron, different body. Hematite: the pigment of Eileen's ochre. The Bedrock Fortress IS iron. The building system: Ore = iron. The seven base materials.

charmDescription: A deep blue charm — the element that gives glass and ceramics their impossible blue
connectedStones: Cobaltite, erythrite, skutterudite; smalt (cobalt blue glass)
questConnection: Oceanianoir Tier 2 reading — Lighthouse lens connection
alchemicalNote: The element of blue. The Lighthouse lens. The Poison Garden's London Blue Topaz. The deep-water zones. The Siren's eye color in the deep. The both are: the adequate — the deep and the blue.

charmDescription: A silvery charm with a faint golden tint — the element of meteorites, the star metal
connectedStones: Millerite, nickeline, garnierite; meteoric iron (kamacite, taenite)
questConnection: Cosmology level — meteorite connection to the Constant
alchemicalNote: The element of meteorites. The stars send metal to earth as nickel-iron alloy. The Constant's starlight crystal. The both are: the adequate — the cosmic and the metallic, the same arrival, different light.

charmDescription: A warm copper casting that develops a green patina over time — the element of the alchemical marriage
connectedStones: Malachite, azurite, turquoise, chrysocolla, bornite, chalcopyrite, cuprite, dioptase
alchemicalNote: THE element of the Inn's architecture. Copper is the alchemical marriage. The charm bracelet chain. The Undercity pipework. Bronze = copper + tin (Atlantis). Verdigris = the patina that matches the bioluminescent algae. The seven base materials: copper is Ore refined. The both are: the adequate — the metal and the patina, the same copper, different time.

charmDescription: A bluish-white casting — the element of brass, the Undercity's fitting
alchemicalNote: The element of brass (copper + zinc). The Undercity's brass fittings. The steampunk aesthetic. The both are: the adequate — the structural and the decorative, the same alloy, different function.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that melts in the hand — the element that flows at body temperature
alchemicalNote: The element that melts at body temperature. The both are: the adequate — the solid and the liquid, the same metal, different temperature. The alchemist's curiosity — a metal that becomes liquid in the hand.

charmDescription: A grey-white metalloid charm — the element of semiconductors, the element between
alchemicalNote: The element between conductor and insulator. The both are: the adequate — the between. The semiconductor: the element that decides. Like the both are: the adequate — the yes and the no, the same switch, different state.

charmDescription: A dark, slightly ominous charm — the element of poison and pigment, the beautiful and the deadly
questConnection: Poison Garden exploration — Artisan Thief's poison knowledge
alchemicalNote: The element of poison and pigment. Orpiment: yellow paint. Realgar: red paint. The Artisan Thief's weaponized knowledge. The both are: the adequate — the beautiful and the deadly, the same element, different dose. The Poison Garden's central element.

charmDescription: A grey charm with a glassy surface — the element that conducts light, the photographic element
questConnection: Poison Garden — photographic connection to Mapplethorpe
alchemicalNote: The element of photography — selenium toning. The Mapplethorpe connection: selenium prints. The both are: the adequate — the poison and the art, the same element, different medium.

charmDescription: A small vial of reddish-brown liquid — the only liquid nonmetal, the element of deep color
alchemicalNote: The only liquid nonmetal at room temperature. The both are: the adequate — the solid and the liquid, the same state, different element. Mercury and bromine: the two liquids.

charmDescription: A tiny glass orb that glows green-white — the noble gas used in high-power lighting
questConnection: Cosmology level — the Lighthouse light connection
alchemicalNote: The noble gas of brilliant light. The Lighthouse's krypton lamp. The both are: the adequate — the noble and the practical, the same gas, different use.

charmDescription: A soft, silvery casting — the element of precise time, the atomic clock element
alchemicalNote: The element of atomic clocks. The both are: the adequate — the reactive metal and the precise time. Rubidium clocks measure time to the nanosecond — the Inn's time system uses rubidium's precision.

charmDescription: A soft silver charm that burns red — the element of fireworks, the element of crimson flame
alchemicalNote: The element of crimson fire. The both are: the adequate — the soft metal and the red flame. Erik's fire: strontium burns the red of Viking war. Celestite: the pale blue stone that contains the red flame.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the rare earth that makes red phosphors, the element of screen-glow
alchemicalNote: The element of red phosphors. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the glowing. Yttrium makes the screens glow red — the Inn's UI uses yttrium's light.

charmDescription: A grey-white charm — the element of zircon, the oldest mineral on earth
alchemicalNote: The element of zircon — the oldest mineral on earth. Zircon crystals hold 4.4 billion years of geological record. The both are: the adequate — the ancient and the present. The Examiner reads zircon to read the earth's memory.

charmDescription: A grey charm that develops an oxide film in iridescent colors — the element of anodized beauty
alchemicalNote: The element of iridescent anodization. The both are: the adequate — the structural metal and the rainbow surface. Like the Shifting Man: the same metal, different color, different day.

charmDescription: A dark grey charm — the element of high-temperature strength, the refractory metal
alchemicalNote: The element of heat resistance. The both are: the adequate — the melting and the enduring. Molybdenite: the soft, greasy mineral that looks like graphite but isn't. Wulfenite: the orange-red crystal of the Poison Garden's edge.

charmDescription: A faintly luminescent charm — the first synthetic element, the element that does not exist in nature
alchemicalNote: The first element that does not exist in nature. The both are: the adequate — the natural and the made. Technetium: the element that had to be created. The star-language implies its existence before humans made it.

charmDescription: A hard, silvery charm — the platinum-group metal of electrical contacts, the hidden connector
alchemicalNote: The hidden platinum-group metal. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the functional. Ruthenium connects the Inn's circuits — the hidden infrastructure of the Undercity.

charmDescription: A brilliant white charm — the most precious metal, the element of mirrors and reflection
connectedStones: Extremely rare in nature; with platinum ores
alchemicalNote: The most precious metal. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the reflective. Rhodium: the mirror's coating. The Owl's gaze. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the element that absorbs hydrogen, the sponge of the periodic table
alchemicalNote: The element that absorbs hydrogen. The both are: the adequate — the metal and the gas, the same absorption, different material. Palladium holds 900 times its volume in hydrogen — the sponge of stars.

charmDescription: A bright silver casting — the element of the moon, the element of mirrors and photography
connectedStones: Argentite, acanthite, native silver, chlorargyrite; in galena as byproduct
alchemicalNote: The element of the moon and mirrors. The both are: the adequate — the sun and the moon (gold and silver). Silver halides: the photographic process. The Mapplethorpe connection: silver prints. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A soft, bluish-white charm — the element of vivid yellow and red pigments, the toxic artist
questConnection: Poison Garden — pigment and art quest
alchemicalNote: The element of cadmium yellow and cadmium red — the artist's most vivid pigments. The both are: the adequate — the beautiful and the toxic. The Poison Garden's art supply. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A very soft silvery charm — the element that cries, the metal that squeaks
connectedStones: Indite (very rare); in sphalerite and cassiterite (trace)
alchemicalNote: The element that cries — indium makes a squeaking sound when bent. The both are: the adequate — the metal and the voice. The Undercity's crying metal.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that may 'tin cry' when bent — the element of bronze, the Atlantis alloy
questConnection: Undercity — bronze = copper + tin for Atlantis architecture
alchemicalNote: The element of bronze. Tin + copper = bronze. The Atlantis architecture. The both are: the adequate — the two metals and the one alloy, the same marriage, different form. The alchemical marriage's other half.

charmDescription: A silvery, brittle charm — the alchemical metal of transformation, the star metal
questConnection: Staircase / alchemy quest — the transformation metal
alchemicalNote: THE alchemical metal. Antimony is the element of the staircase — the transformation principle. Stibnite: the metallic crystal that the alchemists used to make the philosopher's stone. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A brittle, silvery charm — the element of garlic breath, the strange metalloid
alchemicalNote: The element that makes you smell of garlic. The both are: the adequate — the metal and the body. Calaverite: gold telluride — the ore that looks like ordinary rock but contains gold. The deceptive stone.

charmDescription: A dark purple-black crystal charm that sublimes to violet vapor — the element of the sea
alchemicalNote: The element of the sea. Seaweed concentrates iodine. The both are: the adequate — the dark crystal and the purple vapor. The sublimation: the solid that becomes gas without melting — the alchemist's dream.

charmDescription: A glass orb that glows blue-white — the noble gas of brilliant flash, the photographic gas
alchemicalNote: The noble gas of flash photography. The both are: the adequate — the noble and the flash. Xenon flashes: the light that freezes the moment. The Medusa connection — the flash that petrifies.

charmDescription: A gold-tinged liquid metal charm — the element of exact time, the atomic clock
alchemicalNote: The element of the atomic clock. Cesium defines the second. The both are: the adequate — the reactive metal and the precise measure. The Inn's time system: the second is defined by cesium. Persephone's cycles measured in cesium seconds.

charmDescription: A soft silvery charm — the element of the barium swallow, the element that makes things visible
alchemicalNote: The element of medical imaging — barium makes the invisible visible. The both are: the adequate — the opaque and the revealing. Barite: the heavy stone that floats in water because of its density. The Examiner's X-ray.

charmDescription: A silvery charm with a shimmering, color-shifting surface — the first rare earth
questConnection: Staircase / alchemy quest — rare earth series
alchemicalNote: The first rare earth. The beginning of the lanthanide series — the 15 elements that are almost identical, the both are: the adequate — the same and the different. The Inn's rare earths shimmer.

charmDescription: An iron-grey charm that sparks when struck — the rare earth of fire
questConnection: Staircase / alchemy quest — Erik's fire connection
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of fire. Cerium sparks — the lighter flint. The both are: the adequate — the rare earth and the common flame. Erik's fire: cerium is the spark that starts the Viking feast.

charmDescription: A silvery charm with a green tint — the rare earth of green glass
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of green. Praseodymium colors glass yellow-green. The both are: the adequate — the rare earth and the green glass. The Atlantis verdigris connection.

charmDescription: A silvery charm with a pink-purple tint — the rare earth of the strongest magnets
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of the strongest magnets. Neodymium magnets are the strongest permanent magnets. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the attracting. The Inn's magnetism: the lodestone, the compass, the both are: the adequate.

charmDescription: A faintly glowing charm — the rare earth that glows from its own radioactivity, the fire-bringer
connectedStones: None (radioactive, not found in nature in significant amounts)
alchemicalNote: The rare earth that glows. Named after Prometheus, the fire-bringer. The both are: the adequate — the gift and the theft. The element that glows from its own decay — the both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the rare earth of the first magnet, the cobalt magnet
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of the cobalt magnet. Samarium-cobalt magnets: the first rare earth magnets. The both are: the adequate — the rare earth and the magnet. Named after samarskite, named after Colonel Samarsky.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that glows red and blue under UV — the rare earth of phosphors, the euro element
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of phosphors. Europium makes the red phosphor on euro banknotes. The both are: the adequate — the rare earth and the currency. The Inn's anti-counterfeiting: europium glows under UV.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that becomes magnetic when cold — the rare earth of MRI contrast
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of MRI contrast. Gadolinium makes the invisible visible inside the body. The both are: the adequate — the rare earth and the seeing. The Examiner's X-ray, but for the living.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that glows green — the rare earth of green phosphors
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of green phosphors. Terbium green + europium red + blue = white light. The both are: the adequate — the three and the one, the same light, different element.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the rare earth that means 'hard to get', the difficult element
alchemicalNote: The rare earth whose name means 'hard to get'. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the difficult. Dysprosium: the element that resists separation from its neighbors — the lanthanide that clings.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the rare earth with the strongest magnetic moment, the magnetic element
alchemicalNote: The rare earth with the strongest magnetic moment of any element. The both are: the adequate — the small and the magnetic. Holmium: the element that attracts most intensely.

charmDescription: A silvery charm with a pink tint — the rare earth of fiber optics, the signal element
questConnection: Staircase / alchemy quest — fiber optic connection
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of fiber optics. Erbium amplifies light signals in fiber optic cables. The both are: the adequate — the rare earth and the signal. The Inn's communication: the both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the rarest of the stable rare earths, the northern element
alchemicalNote: The rarest of the stable rare earths. Named after Thule, the legendary northern land. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the northern. The Norse zone's rare earth.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the rare earth of atomic clocks, the second clock element
alchemicalNote: The rare earth of the second type of atomic clock. The both are: the adequate — the cesium clock and the ytterbium clock, the same time, different precision. Ytterbium clocks: the next generation.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the last and rarest lanthanide, the hardest rare earth
questConnection: Staircase / alchemy quest — last of the series
alchemicalNote: The last lanthanide. The both are: the adequate — the first (lanthanum) and the last (lutetium). The hardest, densest, rarest of the rare earth series. The end of the lanthanide staircase.

charmDescription: A silvery charm — the element of nuclear control rods, the element that absorbs
connectedStones: Zircon (hafnium is always found with zirconium)
alchemicalNote: The element of nuclear control. Hafnium absorbs neutrons — the element that controls the reaction. The both are: the adequate — the chain and the stop. Always found with zirconium but never separable in nature.

charmDescription: A dark, dense charm — the element of capacitor metals, the element named after Tantalus
alchemicalNote: Named after Tantalus, the mythological figure who could never reach what he desired. The both are: the adequate — the metal and the myth. Tantalum: the element that resists corrosion, the element that endures.

charmDescription: A dense, dark grey charm — the element of the highest melting point, the unmeltable
questConnection: Oceanianoir Tier 2 reading — Erik's fire connection
alchemicalNote: The element with the highest melting point of any metal. The both are: the adequate — the fire and the enduring. Tungsten: the filament of the incandescent bulb — the Lighthouse light's ancestor. Erik's fire cannot melt tungsten.

charmDescription: A dense, dark charm — one of the rarest elements in the earth's crust, the last stable element discovered
alchemicalNote: The last stable element to be discovered (1925). One of the rarest elements in the crust. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the last. Named after the Rhine River. The both are: the adequate.

charmDescription: A dense, bluish charm — the densest element, the heaviest metal
alchemicalNote: The densest element. The both are: the adequate — the small and the heavy. Osmium: the metal that weighs more than any other. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A dense, silvery charm — the element of the asteroid, the K-T boundary marker
connectedStones: With platinum ores; iridium anomaly at K-T boundary
alchemicalNote: The element of the asteroid. The iridium anomaly at the K-T boundary — the global iridium layer that proves the asteroid impact that killed the dinosaurs. The both are: the adequate — the cosmic and the geological, the same iridium, different layer. The Examiner reads the iridium layer.

charmDescription: A dense, silvery-white charm — the noble metal, the element that does not tarnish
connectedStones: Sperrylite (PtAs2), cooperite, native platinum; with osmiridium
alchemicalNote: The noble metal. The both are: the adequate — the precious and the untarnishing. Platinum does not oxidize, does not corrode, does not age. The both are: the adequate — the adequate. The charm bracelet's most precious material.

charmDescription: A warm gold casting — the element of the sun, the alchemist's goal, the metal that does not tarnish
connectedStones: Native gold, calaverite, sylvanite, petzite; in pyrite ('fool's gold') as trace
questConnection: Petrified Forest — Klimt's Golden Phase / catacombs
alchemicalNote: THE element of the catacombs. Gold leaf on dark stone — Klimt's Golden Phase. The alchemist's goal: the philosopher's stone transmutes base metals to gold. The both are: the adequate — the sun and the gold, the same metal, different sky. The building system: gold leaf is a derived material (gold hammered thin).

charmDescription: A small vial of liquid silver — the only liquid metal, the alchemist's mercury, the fluid principle
connectedStones: Cinnabar (HgS, red ore), calomel, native mercury (rare)
questConnection: Poison Garden — alchemical mercury quest, staircase connection
alchemicalNote: THE alchemical fluid. Mercury is the principle of fluidity in alchemy — the liquid that dissolves and unites. Cinnabar: the red ore that bleeds mercury. The both are: the adequate — the solid ore and the liquid metal, the same mercury, different state. The staircase's central element.

charmDescription: A soft, grey charm — the element of poison, the odorless killer
connectedStones: Crookesite, lorandite, thallium in iron pyrites
alchemicalNote: The element of poison. Odorless, tasteless, colorless. The both are: the adequate — the soft and the deadly. The Poison Garden's darkest element — the poison that cannot be detected.

charmDescription: A heavy, dark grey charm — the element of weight, the alchemist's base metal
questConnection: Undercity — the alchemist's base metal, transmutation quest
alchemicalNote: THE alchemist's base metal. Lead is the metal the alchemist transmutes to gold. The both are: the adequate — the heavy and the light, the base and the noble, the same transformation, different stage. Galena: the heavy crystal that is lead ore. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: An iridescent, rainbow-colored charm with a staircase crystal form — the element of geometric beauty
questConnection: Staircase — the geometric crystal, the transformation
alchemicalNote: The element of geometric beauty. Bismuth forms staircase-shaped iridescent crystals. The both are: the adequate — the metal and the staircase. The element that looks like the Inn's staircase — the geometric, iridescent transformation.

charmDescription: A faintly warm charm — the element of radioactive poison, the Curie element
alchemicalNote: Named after Poland by Marie Curie. The element of radioactive poison. The both are: the adequate — the national and the deadly. Polonium: the element that killed Litvinenko — the both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A barely visible charm — the rarest naturally occurring element, the element that barely exists
connectedStones: None (less than 1 gram exists in the entire earth's crust)
alchemicalNote: The rarest naturally occurring element. Less than 1 gram exists in the entire earth's crust at any time. The both are: the adequate — the rare and the barely. The element that barely exists — the both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A glass orb containing an invisible gas — the noble gas that kills, the cave gas
connectedStones: None (radioactive gas, accumulates in caves and basements)
alchemicalNote: The noble gas that kills. Radon accumulates in caves and basements — the geological noble gas. The both are: the adequate — the noble and the deadly, the same gas, different cave. Eileen's cave must be ventilated.

charmDescription: A barely visible charm — the second-rarest element, the most unstable of the first 101
alchemicalNote: The most unstable of the first 101 elements. The both are: the adequate — the reactive and the fleeting. Francium: the element that exists for moments. The both are: the adequate — the adequate.

charmDescription: A faintly glowing charm — the element of the Curies, the element that glows in the dark
questConnection: Catacombs — the glowing element, the Curie connection
alchemicalNote: The element that glows in the dark. Radium: the Curies' discovery. The both are: the adequate — the glowing and the deadly. The element that was put in paint to make watch dials glow — the element that glows is the element that kills. The both are: the adequate.

charmDescription: A faintly glowing charm — the element that defines the actinide series, the first actinide
alchemicalNote: The first actinide. The both are: the adequate — the first and the series. Actinium glows pale blue in the dark — the radioactive luminescence. The beginning of the actinide staircase.

charmDescription: A silvery charm that darkens over time — the element of the Norse god, the alternative nuclear fuel
alchemicalNote: Named after Thor, the Norse god. The both are: the adequate — the god and the element. Thorium: the alternative nuclear fuel — the both are: the adequate — the uranium and the thorium, the same energy, different element. The Norse zone's actinide.

charmDescription: A dense, silvery charm — the rare actinide, the element of decay chains
alchemicalNote: The element of the decay chain. Protactinium sits between thorium and uranium in the radioactive decay chain. The both are: the adequate — the between, the transitional. The element that connects two radioactive giants.

charmDescription: A dense, dark charm that is faintly warm — the element of nuclear power, the geological fuel
connectedStones: Pitchblende (uraninite), autunite, carnotite, tobernite, zircon (trace uranium)
questConnection: Catacombs — the radioactive element, the deep earth fuel
